creating vector drawings, logos and designs

questions.explanation: The Ellipse tool draws ellipses; hold Ctrl for a circle.

Vector images can be enlarged without losing quality, bitmaps become pixelated
Bitmaps are always smaller in file size than vectors
Vectors can only be black and white

questions.stem: Cleaning dust from a computer keyboard and system unit is an example of

re-type all the records from memory

options: Leave cables lying across walkways where they are easy to reach
Avoid eating and drinking near the computers
Open the system unit while it is on

options: increase the speed of the processor
supply power for a short time and protect against sudden power failure
connect the computers to the Internet through the electricity cables

the colour and shape of the icons that represent files
the number of keys on a keyboard

questions.explanation: Direct access gives immediate retrieval of any record.

questions.explanation: Authentication controls access to data.

To change all passwords every hour

all of the data is kept on one disk to avoid any movement between devices
allowing only one user at a time

questions.stem:
(a) List the six stages of information processing in their correct order. [6 marks]
(b) Explain any two methods of data validation. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: data collection
1 mark: data preparation (collation/editing)
1 mark: data input
1 mark: processing
1 mark: output (information)
1 mark: storage
2 marks: range check: ensures values fall between set limits, e.g. age 10 to 25
2 marks: type/format/presence/length check: ensures data is of correct type or format, or is not left blank
questions.explanation: Stages: collection, preparation, input, processing, output, storage (with retrieval/dissemination where taught). Validation methods include range checks, type checks, format checks, presence checks, length checks and check digits.

questions.stem:
(a) Define computer networking. [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between LAN, MAN and WAN. [6 marks]
(c) Name two devices used in setting up a network. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: linking two or more computers and devices to share resources and exchange data
2 marks: LAN: covers a small area such as a building or school
2 marks: MAN: covers a city or town
2 marks: WAN: covers a large area such as a country or continents
1 mark: router / switch
1 mark: hub / network interface card / modem / cables / access point
questions.explanation: Networking links computers to share data and resources. LANs serve a building or campus, MANs a city, WANs countries or the world (the Internet is the largest WAN). Devices include switches, routers, NICs, modems, access points and cabling.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a computer virus? [2 marks]
(b) Name two examples of computer viruses or malware. [2 marks]
(c) State three ways by which a virus can enter a computer. [3 marks]
(d) State three destructive effects of virus infection. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a program written to replicate and cause damage or disruption to a computer system
1 mark: e.g. ILOVEYOU worm / Trojan horse
1 mark: e.g. ransomware (WannaCry) / Melissa / boot-sector virus
1 mark: infected removable storage
1 mark: e-mail attachments and links
1 mark: downloads from untrusted websites / pirated software / networks
1 mark: corrupts or deletes files
1 mark: slows down or crashes the computer
1 mark: steals data / displays unwanted messages / encrypts files for ransom
questions.explanation: A virus is self-replicating malicious code. Examples: ILOVEYOU, Melissa, WannaCry ransomware, Trojans. Entry routes: flash drives, attachments, downloads, pirated software, networks. Effects: corrupted or deleted files, slowness, crashes, data theft, ransom demands.

questions.stem:
(a) Define file organisation. [2 marks]
(b) Describe three types of file organisation. [6 marks]
(c) Give one application suitable for each of two types described. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the way records are arranged on a storage medium so they can be stored and retrieved
2 marks: serial/sequential: records stored one after another (in key order for sequential) and read in order
2 marks: indexed sequential: records in key order with an index allowing direct access
2 marks: random (direct): records placed at addresses calculated from the key and accessed directly
1 mark: sequential: payroll processing
1 mark: random: airline/hotel booking or bank enquiries
questions.explanation: File organisation is how records are arranged for storage and retrieval. Serial/sequential stores records one after another; indexed sequential adds an index for direct access; random/direct uses an address calculated from the key. Payroll suits sequential; reservation systems suit random access.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following terms as used in the relational model: (i) entity; (ii) attribute; (iii) primary key; (iv) foreign key. [8 marks]
(b) State two advantages of the relational database model. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: entity: a person, object or thing about which data is stored, e.g. a student
2 marks: attribute: a property or characteristic of an entity, shown as a column
2 marks: primary key: field whose value uniquely identifies each record in a table
2 marks: foreign key: field in one table that refers to the primary key of another table
1 mark: reduces data redundancy
1 mark: easy to query with SQL / flexible relationships / data integrity
questions.explanation: An entity is a thing about which data is held; attributes are its properties (columns); a primary key uniquely identifies records; a foreign key links to another table's primary key. Advantages: less redundancy, flexibility, integrity and simple querying with SQL.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four careers in data processing and state one duty of each. [8 marks]
(b) Name one professional body for computing practitioners in Nigeria. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: systems analyst: studies and designs information systems
2 marks: programmer: writes, tests and maintains programs
2 marks: database administrator: manages and secures databases
2 marks: computer engineer / network administrator / data entry operator with correct duty
2 marks: Computer Professionals (Registration Council of Nigeria) or Nigeria Computer Society
questions.explanation: Careers include systems analyst (analyses and designs systems), programmer (writes code), database administrator (maintains and secures databases), network administrator (runs networks), computer engineer (builds and repairs hardware) and data entry operator. Professional bodies: CPN and the Nigeria Computer Society.

questions.stem:
(Test of practical work) A cooperative shop records its weekly sales in a spreadsheet:
A2: Rice, B2: 52000, C2: 61000
A3: Beans, B3: 38000, C3: 33500
A4: Garri, B4: 24500, C4: 30000
A5: Palm oil, B5: 41000, C5: 46500
Column B is Week 1 sales (N) and column C is Week 2 sales (N).
(a) Write the formula in D2 to find the total sales of rice for the two weeks, and compute the totals for all four items. [6 marks]
(b) Write the formula in E2 to find the percentage change from Week 1 to Week 2 for rice and compute its value to one decimal place. [4 marks]
(c) Write the formula in D6 to find the grand total and compute its value. [3 marks]
(d) State which item had a fall in sales and by how much. [3 marks]
(e) Describe how to sort the table in descending order of total sales. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: =B2+C2 or =SUM(B2:C2)
1 mark: copy formula down to D5
1 mark: Rice 113000
1 mark: Beans 71500
1 mark: Garri 54500
1 mark: Palm oil 87500
2 marks: =(C2-B2)/B2*100
2 marks: 17.3 per cent
2 marks: =SUM(D2:D5)
1 mark: 326500
2 marks: Beans
1 mark: fell by N4500
1 mark: select A1:D5
1 mark: Data tab > Sort
1 mark: sort by the Total column
1 mark: choose Largest to Smallest and click OK
questions.explanation: Totals: Rice 113000, Beans 71500, Garri 54500, Palm oil 87500; grand total 326500 with =SUM(D2:D5). Rice change = (61000 - 52000) / 52000 x 100 = 17.3%. Beans fell from 38000 to 33500, a drop of N4500. Sort: select the data, Data > Sort, by Total, Largest to Smallest.

questions.stem:
(Test of practical work) A school wants a database of its staff with the fields StaffNo, Surname, FirstName, Department, DateEmployed, Salary.
(a) State a suitable data type for each field. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the steps to create the table in Microsoft Access. [5 marks]
(c) Describe how to create a query that lists only staff in the Science department, and write the criterion. [4 marks]
(d) Describe how to produce a report of all staff sorted by Surname. [3 marks]
(e) State two differences between a table and a query. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: StaffNo: Short Text/AutoNumber
1 mark: Surname: Short Text
1 mark: FirstName: Short Text
1 mark: Department: Short Text
1 mark: DateEmployed: Date/Time
1 mark: Salary: Currency
1 mark: open Access and create a blank database
1 mark: Create > Table Design
1 mark: enter field names and data types
1 mark: set StaffNo as primary key
1 mark: save the table with a name, e.g. STAFF
1 mark: Create > Query Design and add the STAFF table
1 mark: add the required fields to the grid
1 mark: type "Science" in the Criteria row under Department
1 mark: run the query
1 mark: Create > Report Wizard and choose the STAFF table/fields
1 mark: choose Surname as the sort field (ascending)
1 mark: finish and view/print the report
1 mark: a table stores the data permanently
1 mark: a query extracts/selects data from tables based on criteria
questions.explanation: Types: StaffNo Short Text or AutoNumber, names and Department Short Text, DateEmployed Date/Time, Salary Currency. Create a blank database, Create > Table Design, enter fields, set StaffNo as primary key, save. Query Design: add table, fields, Criteria "Science" under Department, Run. Report Wizard: choose fields, sort by Surname, Finish. A table stores data; a query retrieves selected data.

questions.stem:
(Test of practical work) A secretary is to type a two-page notice for a Parents-Teachers Association meeting.
(a) Describe how to start the word processor and open a new blank document. [3 marks]
(b) Describe how to: (i) set all margins to 2.5 cm; (ii) set the font of the whole document to Times New Roman, size 12; (iii) number the agenda items automatically. [9 marks]
(c) Describe how to insert the school name as a footer on both pages. [3 marks]
(d) Describe how to print three copies of only page 2. [3 marks]
(e) State two advantages of a word processor over a typewriter. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: click Start
1 mark: select Microsoft Word (or the word processor)
1 mark: choose Blank document
1 mark: Layout > Margins
1 mark: Custom Margins
1 mark: enter 2.5 cm for top, bottom, left and right and click OK
1 mark: press Ctrl + A to select all
1 mark: choose Times New Roman from the font box
1 mark: choose 12 from the size box
1 mark: select the agenda items
1 mark: Home > Numbering
1 mark: choose a number format
1 mark: Insert > Footer
1 mark: choose a footer style
1 mark: type the school name and close the footer
1 mark: File > Print
1 mark: in Pages box type 2
1 mark: set Copies to 3 and click Print
1 mark: errors can be corrected easily before printing
1 mark: documents can be saved, reused and formatted in many ways
questions.explanation: Start > Word > Blank document. Layout > Margins > Custom Margins, 2.5 cm on all sides. Ctrl + A then Times New Roman, 12. Select agenda items, Home > Numbering. Insert > Footer, type school name. File > Print, Pages: 2, Copies: 3, Print. Word processors allow easy correction, saving, reuse, formatting and multiple copies.
